Lena Brooks (Velocity): Hi CS team — onboarding hit a snag. After ~90s of traffic our embed calls started returning 403 then a burst of 429s. Stack trace shows "token_invalid" then "quota_exceeded: per_key". We're blocked on a demo next week, can you help triage?
Priya Khatri: Sorry to hear that. Quick Qs: which SDK & version? calling via your proxy or direct to our API?
Lena Brooks (Velocity): node client v2.0.3 behind our infra-proxy. We mint tokens with TTL=90s and rotate at 20s before expiry. We also keep the old token for 45s to avoid losing in-flight requests.
Morgan Lee: Keeping the old token that long could double-count auth checks in a short window. Can you paste the auth code / header behavior? small snippet is fine.
Lena Brooks (Velocity): snippet: ```js
{
  tokenTtl: 90,
  refreshBeforeSec: 20,
  oldTokenKeepSec: 45,
  retryPolicy: {attempts: 3, backoffMs: 50}
}
```
Priya Khatri: The backoff and oldTokenKeepSec combo seems risky — the edge may send tokenA and tokenB almost concurrently if your proxy multiplexes requests. Our per-key rate limiter counts auth attempts per distinct session so you can hit the per_key quota quickly.
Lena Brooks (Velocity): Repro trace from their dev env: ```
# first request (t=0) -> 200 OK
HTTP/1.1 200 OK
# at t=85s client swaps, one conn still sends old header -> 403 {"error":"token_invalid"}
# immediately a burst of retries -> 429 {"error":"quota_exceeded","quota":"per_key"}
```
Morgan Lee: Two hypotheses: 1) TTL edge-case where old token considered revoked/expired earlier than expected (clock skew?) 2) overlapping auth attempts + aggressive retries exceed per-key window.
DevOps Bot: Suggested mitigation opened: TEMP-RELAX-PERKEY-1766 (expires in 2h) attached to account Velocity.
Priya Khatri: Suggested customer test: drop oldTokenKeepSec to <=5s and increase retry backoff to >=150ms so retries are spaced. We can temporarily relax per-key enforcement while they run a ramp. Also ask them to ensure NTP sync across proxy hosts.
Lena Brooks (Velocity): I'll flip oldTokenKeepSec to 3s and set backoff 200ms now. One concern: if we lower the keep time we might see rare 401 during long in-flight streams. Is that expected?
Morgan Lee: If you lower to 3s you reduce collision risk. For long streaming requests prefer using the same token for the stream lifetime and rotate only on new connections. That avoids mid-stream swap.
Priya Khatri: Action items: 1) Velocity to run short-grace test and report delta 2) CS to monitor for quota alerts and hold TEMP-RELAX-PERKEY during validation 3) Eng to check auth-introspection logs for that key around 1766010000-1766011300.
Lena Brooks (Velocity): Test run: after change we sustained 5m with no 429s and no 403s during ramp. Will slowly increase traffic. Thanks.
Morgan Lee: Eng note: no server-side revokes during that window; logs show many overlapping token checks before fix. I'll record this in the onboarding playbook under "token swap hazards" and add a CLI reproduce command.
Priya Khatri: Also flagging potential renewal-risk if this had been in the demo window. For enablement: update the onboarding checklist to include token swap guidance and example configs.
Lena Brooks (Velocity): Appreciate the quick help — will share post-ramp status in ~2 hours.
DevOps Bot: Ticket created CS-7910: velocity-auth-swap-triage; labels: onboarding, auth, rate-quota.
Priya Khatri: Closing loop: if ramp is stable, we'll remove TEMP-RELAX-PERKEY and update docs. If not, eng will instrument more fine-grained per-session telemetry. Thanks team. :rocket:
